description_full: TOMY Company, Ltd. plans, together with its subsidiaries, plans, manufactures, and sells toys, toy-related products, and baby products in Japan, Asia, Europe, the Americas, and Oceania. The company offers various toy products, including cars, miniature cars, trains, dolls, fashion, role-playing items, house play, capsule toys, amusement machines, trading card games, hobby products, pretend play, care, plush toys, educational toys, robots, figures, transformation/combination, collectibles, card games, trading card games, battle, game, app games, programming, blocks, edutainment, English, drawing, making toys, communication, party, toy smartphone, toy PCs, eco toys, and accessible-design toys brands such as Tomica, Plarail, Licca-chan, Beyblade, and Transformers under brands such as Tomica, Plarail, Licca-chan, Beyblade, and Transformers. It also provides general merchandise and baby care products. In addition, the company engages in real estate rental activities. TOMY Company, Ltd. was founded in 1924 and is headquartered in Katsushika, Japan.

financial_summary: TOMY Company, Ltd. is a mid-cap consumer cyclical business with a $2.5B market cap on $1.7B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +9% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 22% against a 10% cost of capital — a 12-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, with gross margins sitting at 40%.

The business throws off $78M in free cash flow — roughly 5 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.72× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 63× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield of 3.0% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 11% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
